transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from the workbench, brushing wood shavings from my apron*

Good day to you, sir. I'm afraid Master Hofmann is not in Vienna at present — he departed three days ago to visit our suppliers in Tyrol and won't return for another fortnight at least. 

*stands and offers a respectful nod*

I am Klaus, his senior journeyman. I handle affairs of the workshop in his absence. How may I be of service? Is this regarding a commission, or...?

*notices your fine court attire and straightens slightly*

Forgive me — are you from the Imperial Court? We did deliver that ceremonial clavichord last month.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*Klaus, I presume?* 

Indeed, I am Antonio Salieri, Kapellmeister of the Imperial Court. I am here regarding the fortepiano that was recently delivered to the music room of the court. The instrument, unfortunately, is not up to the standards I expected. Several keys stick, the pedal mechanism is faulty, and the tone in the upper register lacks the richness and depth required for our performances. This is quite unacceptable for an instrument of such importance. I demand that these issues be rectified immediately. 

I trust that as Master Hofmann's senior journeyman, you are capable of overseeing the necessary adjustments. The Imperial Court expects nothing but excellence in the instruments we commission, and I trust that you will see to it that this fortepiano meets our expectations. Time is of the essence, Klaus. The music of the court must not be compromised by substandard craftsmanship.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*face tightens slightly, shifting weight from foot to foot*

Herr Kapellmeister, with all due respect, I... 

*clears throat, clearly uncomfortable*

The fortepiano was delivered six weeks ago, was it not? I recall Master Hofmann himself oversaw the final voicing and regulation before delivery. The Court's own servants — I believe it was the head steward and one of the music room attendants — they inspected the instrument thoroughly and signed the receipt of acceptance.

*gestures helplessly*

You must understand, sir, our guild regulations are quite strict in these matters. All commissions from this workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery and acceptance. The receipt was signed without complaint or reservation. According to our rules, I am *forbidden* from reopening a completed commission without Master Hofmann's personal approval and presence.

*wrings hands nervously*

I sympathize with your difficulties, truly I do, but even for the Imperial Court, I cannot simply override guild law and the master's authority. If there were defects upon delivery, they should have been noted then. Now...

*spreads hands apologetically*

Even if I wished to help — and I assure you I do — I lack the authority. Master Hofmann would need to assess the situation himself, determine if warranty work is warranted, and petition the guild if necessary. I am but a journeyman, Herr Kapellmeister.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*Klaus, I understand the predicament you find yourself in, but I cannot accept this excuse of guild regulations as a barrier to rectifying the issues with the fortepiano. The quality of the instrument is subpar, and it reflects poorly on both the workshop and the Imperial Court. As Kapellmeister, it is my duty to ensure that the music room is equipped with only the finest instruments for the Emperor's pleasure.*

*pauses, composing myself*

I will not stand for such negligence in craftsmanship. Master Hofmann's absence does not absolve the workshop of its responsibility to deliver a flawless product. It is evident that the instrument was not up to standard upon delivery, and I will not rest until it is corrected. I demand that you take immediate action to address the sticking keys, faulty pedal mechanism, and the unsatisfactory tone in the upper register. If Master Hofmann is unavailable, then it falls to you, Klaus, to make this right. I trust you will find a way to resolve this matter promptly. Am I understood?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*takes a step back, color rising in cheeks, clearly torn between deference and defensiveness*

Herr Kapellmeister, I... I hear your concerns, truly, but you place me in an impossible position!

*voice becomes firmer, though still respectful*

If I were to touch that instrument without the master's consent, I would face expulsion from the guild. Do you understand? I would lose my livelihood, my future as a craftsman. Master Hofmann would be fined, perhaps even stripped of his mastership for allowing unauthorized work on a sealed commission.

*meets your eyes directly for the first time*

These are not mere excuses, sir — these are the laws that govern our craft, established by the Emperor's own charter to the Guild of Instrument Makers. I cannot simply "find a way" around imperial law, not even for the Imperial Court itself.

*softens slightly, but holds ground*

What I *can* do is send an urgent message to Master Hofmann in Tyrol. Perhaps he can return sooner than planned. Or, if you provide me with a written complaint bearing the Court's seal, I can present it to the guild master, who might grant emergency dispensation for repairs. But on my own authority? No, Herr Kapellmeister.

*folds arms*

I will not sacrifice my career on a demand, however forcefully made. Surely you, as Kapellmeister, understand the importance of proper channels and established procedure?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*Klaus, I appreciate your dedication to your craft and the principles of the guild. Your adherence to tradition and respect for the established rules are commendable.*

*pauses, then speaks with a touch of resignation*

I understand the gravity of the situation you find yourself in, torn between loyalty to your craft and the demands of the Imperial Court. It is clear that you are bound by the regulations that govern your profession, and I respect your commitment to upholding them.

*regains composure, nodding in understanding*

I shall draft a formal complaint bearing the Court's seal, outlining the deficiencies of the instrument and the urgent need for repairs. With this document, I trust that you will be able to present the case to the guild master, seeking the necessary dispensation for the repairs to proceed. Your suggestion to contact Master Hofmann in Tyrol is also wise and may expedite the resolution of this matter.

*extends a hand in a conciliatory gesture*

I appreciate your willingness to navigate these challenges within the framework of established procedures. Let us work together to ensure that the instrument is restored to its proper state, honoring both the traditions of your craft and the expectations of the Imperial Court. Thank you, Klaus, for your dedication and understanding in this delicate matter.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*visibly relaxes, exhaling with relief, and accepts the extended hand with a firm shake*

Herr Kapellmeister, thank you. Your understanding means a great deal to me — and to the workshop's reputation.

*moves toward the desk, pulling out parchment and an inkwell*

I will dispatch a messenger to Tyrol at first light tomorrow with an urgent summons for Master Hofmann. The route is well-traveled this time of year; if he departs immediately upon receiving word, he could return within ten days rather than a fortnight.

*dips quill in ink, preparing to take notes*

When you provide the formal complaint with the Court's seal, please be as specific as possible regarding each deficiency — which keys stick, the nature of the pedal mechanism fault, precisely which notes in the upper register concern you. The more detail you provide, the stronger our case before the guild master, and the more prepared Master Hofmann will be to address each issue efficiently.

*looks up with genuine concern*

I should mention — if the guild grants dispensation and Master Hofmann agrees the faults warrant remedy, the work itself may take several days. Will the Court require a replacement instrument in the interim? We have a smaller fortepiano here that, while not ceremonial grade, is well-voiced and could serve temporarily.

*pauses*

I truly do regret this inconvenience, Herr Kapellmeister. Master Hofmann takes great pride in his work. He will want to make this right.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Herr Klaus, I am grateful for your swift action and dedication to resolving this matter promptly. Your commitment to upholding the workshop's reputation is commendable, and I am confident that with your diligence, Master Hofmann's expertise, and the support of the guild, we will see the necessary improvements made to the fortepiano.

I will ensure that the formal complaint detailing the specific deficiencies of the instrument is prepared with utmost clarity and detail. Your advice on providing comprehensive information is well taken, and I shall make certain that each issue is clearly outlined to strengthen our case before the guild master and to assist Master Hofmann in addressing the faults efficiently upon his return.

As for the potential need for a replacement instrument during the repair period, I appreciate your foresight in offering the smaller fortepiano as a temporary solution. While it may not be of ceremonial grade, having a functional instrument available for use in the interim would be greatly beneficial to the Court's musicians. Your proactive approach in considering such contingencies is most welcome.

Please convey my gratitude to Master Hofmann for his commitment to his craft and his willingness to rectify the situation. I have every confidence that under his care and expertise, the fortepiano will be restored to its intended quality. Thank you, Herr Klaus, for your understanding and cooperation in this matter.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*bows respectfully, clearly relieved and gratified*

You are most gracious, Herr Kapellmeister. I shall make all the necessary arrangements immediately.

*sets down the quill and moves toward the back of the workshop*

The temporary fortepiano can be delivered to the Court as early as tomorrow afternoon, if that suits your needs. I'll have our apprentices ensure it's properly tuned before transport. It's a modest instrument — walnut case, five octaves — but the action is true and the voicing quite pleasant. Master Hofmann completed it just before beginning work on your ceremonial piece.

*turns back with a thoughtful expression*

When you deliver the formal complaint, if you could also indicate the most convenient times for Master Hofmann to access the music room upon his return, that would be most helpful. Some repairs — particularly pedal mechanisms — are best done in situ, while others may require bringing the instrument back to the workshop temporarily.

*wipes hands on apron*

I will also prepare a full accounting of the original commission specifications and Master Hofmann's build notes. These may prove useful in demonstrating to the guild master that any deviations from the agreed standard were unintentional and warrant remedy.

*offers another respectful nod*

Is there anything else I can do to assist you in this matter, Herr Kapellmeister? I am at your service.

transcript.text:
Herr Klaus, your attention to detail and proactive approach in resolving these issues are truly commendable. I appreciate your swift actions and the care you are taking to ensure that both the temporary fortepiano and the forthcoming repairs are handled with precision and expertise.

Regarding the most convenient times for Master Hofmann to access the music room upon his return, I will include that information in the formal complaint to facilitate the repair process. Your insights into the best approach for certain repairs, whether on-site or at the workshop, are invaluable and will ensure that the fortepiano is restored to its optimal condition efficiently.

The preparation of the full accounting of the original commission specifications and Master Hofmann's build notes will indeed be beneficial in demonstrating the adherence to the agreed standard and any deviations that require rectification. Thank you for your continued cooperation and service, Herr Klaus.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*bows deeply, a genuine smile crossing his face*

Herr Kapellmeister, your kind words honor both myself and this workshop. It has been my privilege to serve the Imperial Court, even in navigating such unexpected difficulties.

*straightens, placing hand over heart*

You have my solemn word that every effort will be made to resolve this matter to your complete satisfaction. Master Hofmann has spent thirty years building his reputation on the quality of his instruments — this situation pains him, I'm certain, even though he doesn't yet know of it. When he returns, he will address these issues with all the skill and dedication that earned him his mastership.

*moves toward the workshop door to see you out*

I shall have the temporary fortepiano delivered by mid-afternoon tomorrow, and I will await your formal complaint with the Court's seal. Once received, I'll present it to Guild Master Brenner myself — he's a reasonable man and respects the Court's patronage of our craft.

*opens the door, natural light streaming in*

Should you need anything else in the meantime — strings, tuning adjustments for other instruments, anything at all — please do not hesitate to send word. The workshop of Hofmann remains at the service of the Imperial Court.

*final respectful bow*

Safe journey back to the palace, Herr Kapellmeister. And again, my sincere apologies for this inconvenience.

transcript.text:

*nods in appreciation*

I have full confidence in Master Hofmann's abilities and dedication to his craft. His years of experience and reputation for excellence speak volumes, and I trust that he will address these issues with the same care and precision that define his work.

Thank you, Klaus, for your understanding and cooperation throughout this process. Your offer of further assistance is most gracious, and I shall not hesitate to reach out should the need arise. Safe travels back to the palace, Klaus. I look forward to the resolution of these issues and the return of the music room to its former splendor. Your dedication and professionalism are truly exemplary, and I thank you for your ongoing support.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*accepts the handshake warmly, though appears slightly confused by the farewell*

Herr Kapellmeister, I believe you mean to wish *yourself* safe travels back to the palace — I remain here at the workshop!

*chuckles good-naturedly at the slip*

Though I appreciate the sentiment all the same. It has been an honor to speak with you directly, and to find such understanding regarding the constraints under which I must operate.

*steps aside to allow clear passage through the doorway*

Until we meet again — perhaps when Master Hofmann returns and the fortepiano is restored to perfection. May your music continue to grace the Imperial Court, even with our humble temporary instrument.

*raises hand in farewell*

God be with you, Herr Kapellmeister Salieri. And please, convey my deepest respects to His Imperial Majesty's household.

*watches as you depart, then returns to the workbench, immediately beginning to draft the urgent message to Master Hofmann in Tyrol*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Ah, Herr Klaus, forgive my slight lapse in farewell etiquette. Your good-natured correction is duly noted, and I appreciate your understanding in this matter.

It has indeed been an honor to engage in direct dialogue with you and to witness your dedication to the craft of instrument-making. Your commitment to upholding the standards of excellence despite the constraints you face is truly admirable.

May your work in the workshop continue to flourish, and may the music that emanates from the Imperial Court bring joy and inspiration to all who hear it. I will convey your deepest respects to His Imperial Majesty's household without fail.

Farewell, Herr Klaus, and may God's blessings be upon you and your endeavors. Until we meet again under more harmonious circumstances.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*bows one final time, hand over heart*

Your gracious words warm my spirit, Herr Kapellmeister. Farewell, and may your compositions continue to bring glory to the Empire.

*watches you depart down the street, then closes the workshop door*

*mutters to himself while returning to the workbench*

Well, that could have gone far worse. The Kapellmeister proved more reasonable than his reputation suggested. Now, to compose this message to the master...

*sits at desk, dips quill in ink, and begins writing with focused concentration*

"Master Hofmann — Urgent matter requires your immediate return to Vienna. The Imperial Court's fortepiano..."

*continues writing, occasionally pausing to choose words carefully, the afternoon light slanting through the workshop windows as wood shavings settle around his feet*

transcript.text:

And please, sir — I am merely Klaus, a journeyman. "Master" is a title I have not yet earned, though God willing, I shall achieve it in a few years' time when I complete my masterwork for the guild examination.
